title: Effects of High-Intensity Laser Therapy as complementary treatment for orthopaedic rehabilitation in non-specific chronic back pain
summary: For many orthopaedic diseases, irradiation with LASER light in the low energy range is already successfully used to improve the symptoms of pain. Recent studies have also shown that the use of LASER therapy with a high dose of energy (high intensity laser therapy) can have a beneficial effect not only on pain, but also on the range of movement and function of the lumbar spine in chronic back problems. Research on a complementary LASER therapy with high energy output within an orthopaedic rehabilitation is not yet available. This is what this study is now intended to investigate. In order to achieve a high significance, rehabilitants of the Lahntalklinik with non-specific chronic back pain are randomly divided into two groups: Both groups receive the treatment program of the Lahntalklinik prescribed by the receiving ward physician and individually adapted to the clinical picture. Group 1 additionally receives a LASER therapy with effective high energy output and Group 2 additionally receives a LASER treatment without energy output (placebo therapy). The aim of the study is to investigate whether the supplemental LASER therapy in the high energy range exerts an effect on pain, range of movement and everyday function in rehabilitants with chronic back pain that goes beyond the placebo effect.

interventions.name: Patients with non-specific chronic back pain receiving high-intensity laser therapy in addition to orthopaedic rehabilitation treatment.
Patients with non-specific chronic back pain receiving placebo laser therapy in addition to orthopaedic rehabilitation treatment.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Non-specific chronic back pain, age 18-65 years
Exclusion criteria:
Follow-up treatment, skin diseases and haematomas in the irradiation area, pregnancy, heavy menstruation, acute internal or acute infectious diseases, tumours, pacemakers
